example_programs.title: Piano
example_programs.description: A little sound instrument controlled by keyboard letters. This short program is a good first complete listing. DATA assigns modulation to each letter; the buzzer makes effects rather than precisely pitched musical notes.
example_programs.controls: **To play:** press letters **A to Z**. **Return** ends the program. Try keys, then change a DATA value to compare sounds.
example_programs.learning: DIM reserves an array, READ fills it, INKEY reads keys and SOUND makes sound.

illustrations.caption: Piano in Studio: letters A to Z become a little sound instrument.

example_programs.title: Pocket Duel
example_programs.description: Two characters fight in a thirty-two-cell arena whose left edge joins the right. Mines and fences complicate movement; little triangles show health and the lower line shows available charge. The game uses only LCD and buzzer.
example_programs.controls: **Controls:** left/right arrows move; **lowercase A** attacks a neighbour; **Space** teleports; **Return** ends. Attack and teleport need full charge. The opponent acts after your action.
example_programs.learning: LCDCHAR defines characters, LOCATE avoids full redraws, LCDTRI and LCDLINE show gauges; INKEY, conditions and subroutines organise play.

illustrations.caption: Pocket Duel in Studio: characters, obstacles, health and charge share thirty-two LCD cells.

example_programs.title: Orbital Duel
example_programs.description: A space battle inspired by Battleship. Command three satellite formations of three, two and two cells on a six-by-six grid. Canon has the same fleet; the first to hit all seven enemy cells wins. Satellites and shots remain visible on paper.
example_programs.controls: **To play:** Return at the welcome screen; enter a starting cell such as **A1**, then **H** for a formation extending right or **V** extending down. Enter shots **A1 to F6**, or **Q** to quit. The left grid holds your satellites; the right records shots. Let the program position the paper.
example_programs.learning: LINE builds grids; GLYPH prints satellites, shots and explosions; arrays, randomness and logical tests manage positions and enemy decisions.

illustrations.caption: The LCD requests the next shot while both grids remain on paper.
Explanatory game diagram: your satellites on the left, a B4 miss and B2 hit. The three patterns reproduce the program DATA.

example_programs.title: Ballistic Duel
example_programs.description: Two cannons face each other across terrain printed once. Choose angle and power: a dotted trajectory appears and impacts accumulate. The terrain stays fixed; previous shot values print below the arena. Play against Canon or another player.
example_programs.controls: **To play:** enter a seed from **1 to 9999**, then **1** against Canon or **2** for two players. Supply the requested angle and power **20 to 100**. Zero angle ends play. Reuse a seed for the same terrain; save your program before loading the game.
example_programs.learning: RANDOMIZE and RND prepare terrain; a sine table and successive additions speed trajectories; BOX, LINE, DRAW and motors compose the sheet.

illustrations.caption: The LCD asks player two for an angle.
Paper simulated from the ROM-executed program: fixed terrain, dotted shots, impacts and printed history.
